_comment: THE DEPLOYED SCHEDULE, AS ONE REVIEWABLE RECORD.
Three artifacts must agree on the Cloudflare Worker's TRIGGERS:
* deploy/wrangler.toml  [triggers] crons  -- what wrangler actually applies
* deploy/cloudflare-worker.js  CRON_DISPATCHER -- what scheduled() dispatches on
* this file -- the committed, human-reviewable statement of both
Check 16 in tests/workflows/test_workflow_lint.py compares all three as sets
and recomputes expected_invocations_per_day from the crons below, so this
file cannot drift away from the deployment without a red suite. That is why
no interval is restated in a workflow comment anywhere in this repository: a
number in prose is the drift class that produced breaking-monitor.yml's
stale 'every 5 min' header, which survived because the only check that
looked at it PRINTED the contradiction to a log nobody read.
ONE TRIGGER, NOT FIVE. The account hit Cloudflare's Workers Free limit of
5 cron triggers per account (code 10072) and the deploy HALF-APPLIED: the
code shipped, the 40 1 / 40 13 re-fire crons never registered. The jobs were
merged into one dispatcher rather than upgrading the plan.
expected_invocations_per_day is what CLOUDFLARE INVOKES, one term per cron:
* * * * *    -> 60 fires/hour x 24 h = 1440  (the dispatcher)
TOTAL        = 1440
1440 > the 1228 the five-cron schedule intended, and that is the honest
cost of merging on the free tier: 1440 invocations a day against a free
allowance of 100,000. It buys the schedule below without touching the plan.
expected_internal_job_fires_per_day is what the DISPATCHER DECIDES, and it
is the figure that must not move -- it is the pre-merge cadence, term by term:
*/3 * * * *   -> 20 fires/hour x 24 h = 480 (the BREAKING sweep)
*/2 * * * *   -> 30 fires/hour x 24 h = 720  (academic sweep)
17 * * * *    ->  1 fire/hour x 24 h      =  24  (heartbeat health check)
35 1 * * *    ->  1 fire/day              =   1  (morning digest)
35 13 * * *   ->  1 fire/day              =   1  (evening digest)
re-fire x4    ->  4 fires/day per slot    =   8  (40/45/50/55, both slots)
prebuild x2   ->  1 fire/day per slot    =   2  (55 0 / 55 12 -- U9)
ladder x3     ->  3 fires/hour x 24 h     =  72  (17/32/47 -- U10, was a GitHub cron)
THE PREBUILD IS TWO MORE JOB FIRES ON THE SAME GRID, NOT TWO MORE TRIGGERS.
GitHub-hosted SCHEDULED runs were measured 4.5-7h late across 96 daily-news
firings (2026-08-29 to 2026-10-12, mean 306.8 min, max 708.3 min), while
workflow_dispatch created a run in ~2s across 90 dispatched runs. So the
prebuild is now requested by THIS Worker's clock at 06:40 / 18:40 NPT, which
is 40 minutes ahead of the 07:20 / 19:20 digest slots. That is 2 more job
fires on the one existing `* * * * *` trigger, so expected_invocations_per_day
does NOT move: a minute that already ran a sweep just also dispatches.
The sweeps are 480 and 720 and NOT the other way round: `*/3` is the
BREAKING sweep and `*/2` is the ACADEMIC one. Read the code, not the names.
1234 against the pre-merge 1228 is +6: the digest re-fire went from ONE
extra firing per slot to a BOUNDED WINDOW of four (slot+5/+10/+15/+20
minutes), which is the retry that could not register when the deploy
half-applied. The window closes at 01:55 / 13:55 UTC, ten minutes before the
02:05 UTC GitHub fallback in daily-news.yml (07:50 NPT) owns the slot: two
arms racing every bad day would be a second push by construction.
+2 MORE AGAIN FOR THE PREBUILD (1234 -> 1236), and these fire at 00:55 /
12:55 UTC -- OUTSIDE both digest hours (01 and 13), so they cannot collide
with a slot instant or a re-fire window entry.
THE PREBUILD IS ASKED FOR, NOT WAITED ON, AND THAT IS THE FAIL-SAFE. The
dispatcher dispatches digest-prebuild.yml and returns; it writes no KV key,
records no delivery marker and reads no ledger. So nothing a prebuild does
can change what the digest cron does 40 minutes later. A prebuild that fails,
or is still running when the slot arrives, leaves NO sealed artifact, and the
EXISTING fallback ladder takes over unchanged: an immediate push plus
escalateToActions dispatching a full build. The worst case of this feature is
the behaviour that existed before it -- one push about 22 minutes late. It is
never 'no news', and it never double-fires, because the prebuild job only
seals; the single push belongs to the digest cron.
426 of the 1440 ticks a day have nothing due. A tick like that costs one
clock comparison and makes NO KV read and NO KV write, which is why merging
five crons into one did not move the KV budget below by a single key. The two
prebuild minutes (00:55, 12:55) are divisible by NEITHER the 2-minute sweep
NOR the 3-minute one and are not :17, so each was a no-op tick before and is
a work tick now: work_ticks 988 -> 990 and no_op_ticks 452 -> 450. The
ladder's three minutes add 72 JOB FIRES but only 24 WORK TICKS: :17 is
already the health check and :32 already the academic sweep, so only the :47
minute moves -- work 990 -> 1014 and no_op 450 -> 426. Invocations stay 1440
throughout: every addition here rides the ONE deployed trigger.
JOB FIRES AND TICKS ARE DIFFERENT NUMBERS AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE POINT.
1014 ticks do work and 426 do not, which is the 1440 Cloudflare invokes. On
some of those 1014 more than one job runs (a minute divisible by 6 runs both
sweeps, and a minute divisible by 3 that is even runs the sweep plus, at
01:40, the digest re-fire), so 1308 jobs fit inside 1014 ticks. Check 16
recomputes all three and requires work_ticks + no_op_ticks = 1440.
THE RE-FIRE IS NOT A SECOND DELIVERY. Cloudflare cron START JITTER is
unbounded from the inside: the 01:35 tick can genuinely begin at 01:47, and
nothing in the Worker can prevent it. Each later tick in the window fires
the same slot again, and the delivery ledger's `ntfy_sent_at` check turns
that into one KV read and no network call. They add invocations and zero
steady-state KV writes.
THE DELIVERY GUARANTEE IS AT-LEAST-ONCE with a possible duplicate on the
recovery path only. It is NOT exactly-once: ntfy does not deduplicate a
caller-supplied message id (measured live -- 10 POSTs, 10 messages, HTTP
200 every time), and there is no transaction spanning 'ntfy has the
message' and 'KV has the record'. Do not let any doc say otherwise.
KV WRITES PER DAY ARE A COMPUTED ASSERTION, NOT A COMMENT. The digest arm's
figures are re-derived by tests/digest/digest_delivery.test.js, which
measures one real delivery with the harness's own counters and requires
this table to agree; the totals are re-derived from the terms next to them
by Check 16 in tests/workflows/test_workflow_lint.py. A budget kept only in
prose starts lying the first time a line of code is added, and nobody
notices until the free tier quietly stops being free.
ledger_writes = 4, NOT 2, AND THAT IS NOT A TYPO: one delivered slot
writes the ledger TWICE -- `pending` before the POST and `sent` after it --
and the write-ahead ordering is the guard against losing a send outright.
2 slots x 2 writes = 4. Recording 2 here would have been the exact lie
this section exists to prevent.
THE BUDGET DID NOT MOVE WHEN THE CRONS MERGED. The heartbeat writes are
throttled to one per 30 minutes, so their count is set by the CLOCK and not
by how many triggers deliver them: 48 breaking + 48 academic whatever the
trigger count, because the dispatcher reproduces the same sweep instants.
health_url is the ?health=1 endpoint both the digest-watchdog arm and the
drift canary poll. It lives here rather than in two workflow literals so
there is exactly ONE place to correct a subdomain -- and Check 16 asserts
both workflows use this exact string.
The logical schedule ONE trigger reproduces. NOT deployed crons -- there
is exactly one of those above. This is the record the cadence-parity test
compares against the pre-merge schedule over a simulated day, so a change
to any of these that alters when a job fires fails that test.
THE PUNCTUAL PREBUILD TRIGGER. GitHub-hosted SCHEDULED runs are
measured 4.5-7h late (96 daily-news firings 2026-08-29..2026-10-12,
mean 306.8 min, max 708.3 min); workflow_dispatch creates a run in
~2s (90 runs). digest-prebuild.yml already had a workflow_dispatch
trigger with a `digest_time` choice input and already did
dispatch->wait->seal. Only the TRIGGER was broken.
So the Worker asks for it on its own clock, 40 minutes before each
digest slot. 06:40 NPT gives a prebuild whose 5-9 min measured duration
(22 min on one run) is comfortably inside the margin; measured duration
and the margin must BOTH be checked, because a prebuild that overruns
must degrade and not block.
`prebuild_lead_minutes` is the design choice and it is DERIVED, not
restated: the Worker computes slot - lead. These two crons below are
what that arithmetic produces, and Check 16 plus the NPT table in
tests/workflows/test_workflow_lint.py hold both the expression and its
Nepal Time (06:40 / 18:40 NPT).
THESE ARE NOT CLOUDARE TRIGGERS. They ride the one deployed
`* * * * *`, exactly like the sweeps and the digest slots.
digest_prebuild.on_failure: the digest cron finds no sealed artifact and the existing fallback ladder owns the slot: an immediate push plus escalateToActions dispatching a full build, i.e. one push ~22 min late rather than no news

_comment: THE EMPTY-DIGEST RETRY LADDER, MOVED OFF GITHUB'S SCHEDULER 2026-10-20.
It was digest-watchdog.yml's second cron, `17,32,47 * * * *` -- 72
firings a day, each a BILLED runner whose only work was to read
state/digest_retry.json and, almost always, find nothing due (the ladder's
own gates are +15 then +45 minutes after an empty digest, so at most two
retries exist per ladder). The Worker already ticks every minute, so the
same phase is now a branch of planTickFor() and a check costs a KV read.
THE SCHEDULE DID NOT MOVE, ONLY WHO PAYS. :17/:32/:47 every hour, the same
instants the GitHub cron fired on, so a retry is never early or late by
more than it was before. `every_minutes` and `phase_minute` are checked
against the Worker's own SCHED_LADDER_EVERY_MIN / SCHED_LADDER_PHASE, and
`fire_minutes` is DERIVED from them rather than hand-written -- the Worker
computes its own list the same way, so a literal here would be a second
opinion that can drift.
THE WORKFLOW STILL DOES THE WORK. This arm dials digest-watchdog.yml with
ladder_only=true and nothing else. That job owns the ladder's gates, its
ledger and its ntfy alert. The Worker does NOT touch
state/digest_retry.json and does NOT dispatch daily-news.yml.
72 JOB FIRES, 24 NEW WORK TICKS. The three minutes are :17 (already the
health check), :32 (already the academic sweep) and :47 (a no-op until
now), so only the :47 minute changes the tick profile: work +24, no-op
-24. Invocations do not move -- it rides the one deployed trigger.
A DUE RETRY THAT IS MISSED IS LATE, NOT LOST: the next ladder tick tries
again at most 15 minutes later, the KV debounce is keyed on the attempt
number so each rung is dialled once, and the 04/16 watchdog pair still
runs the job regardless.
digest_ladder.on_failure: a due retry is not dialled until the next ladder tick (at most 15 min later); the 04/16 watchdog pair still runs the job and the Worker never touches state/digest_retry.json, so the ladder is late, never lost
